title: What is the definition for AI slop?
author: No_Departure7494
selftext:
It's kind of demotivating to see people post their WIPS on here, whether it be a rough sketch for a game, testing a mechanic or what have you and then the inevitable comments start. "You wasted compute for this bruh?", "Shit just looks like slop to me bruh".

It's a phrase any idiot can say with no real meaning behind it. Is the goal of AI game development to it get right 100% of the time or to experiment and have fun with such a nascent technology?

This is the tech bro version of calling people goyim.

comments.author: Shuma665
comments.body:
"It's like porn you know it when you see it."  To me it's  something that clearly hasn't had enough human oversight, direction and love.  The reason i use the art / porn quote is because AI doesn't have a sense of 'taste or style'  per say.   Which is why so much slop is visible as humans have grown up around things that have, at least trivally, been curated/created by a human.    

Right now i'm working on a project and the systems are good the art is good, all AI assisted, and me reviewed, refined, and approved.   But the dialog. woof.  it's slop as i have given it no love.

comments.author: riccioverde11
comments.body:
It's practically low effort. People who never worked in the industry or anyway not in software can't comprehend. So the first thing that ai spits out is probably slop. To the untrained or noobs might look super cool, but probably it's slop. 
So you take that super cool in your mind, show it to people, and you think you discovered the moon .
That's slop for you.
I think it's the equivalent of your best friend cooking this super special meal for you, and it's pure bread. You feel cheated.

It's not a game at that point, unless you're building snake or pong or some shit. Everything posted here is just trailer garbage. A few half-baked mechanics is not a game. A real game has seriously thought out mechanics and you need to basically polish all AI slop from the visuals before you release it. SFX? Also takes several hours unless you want dogshit SFX.

comments.author: Due_Answer_4230
comments.body: AI slop is sloppy work. That's all there is to it. There is a lot of human slop on steam and there was long before chatgpt happened. It's just easier to create sloppy work now, so a lot of people do it. It is possible to try hard and really care and still turn out sloppy work btw - with or without AI. Think of it like making a wooden chair. You can try hard and use the best tools, but there is a lot more than effort and tool choice that goes into fine woodworking.

comments.author: AkiraVero
comments.body:
To me, AI slop is when someone aggressively promotes a game, acting like it’s a finished product, when they’ve put little effort into it and it isn’t ready to be marketed: a Steam page, a trailer, a community push / trying to act oblivious and high when in reality they know exactly what they are doing, they just don’t care. They have no business marketing it to me.

I enjoy WIPs, even “one-shot prompt” experiments, when the person is genuine and not trying to sell me something: They know there’s a long way to go, or it’s just for fun to see what an "AI can do".

And of course, it's clear when effort and love is actually put into something or they have put a lot of thought into the design of what they are trying to build, and I would never associate that word to something like that

I just don't like the term in general, but it can be interpreted in a lot of different ways as you can see by the comments here.

comments.author: AfroJimbo
comments.body:
I think people are overcomplicating it. 

Slop means generating anything with a prompt, getting the average result from the tool (image, video, code, text), and not doing anything else.  Just prompt and done without quality checking or going any further to improve the output.

Hell, I'd refine it a little further and say that the prompt matters, too, because with better prompting and context/intent, it's possible to get decent and different output from a single prompt.

But slop is putting in very little effort in the input and accepting very average or poor output. 

Anything behind that, imo, and now we're just discussing personal taste.

comments.author: harmonicrain
comments.body: I think the issue is people get too excited by their own projects before they're ready for most eyes to see them.

comments.author: Evile_Gaming
comments.body:
u/Fuzzzy420 This guy gets it. There's a lot of 'one shot' crap.  
Building anything more meaningful than a 30 second tech demo; You know where the UI isn't 'Astra Teal' or the sprites jank all over the place like an epileptic cat in a tumble drier. Or it has a tech tree with 300 branches, and not a single talent has been thought about.  
  
A good games till takes time and craft, and takes blowing out 5 hour limits on multiple accounts, for weeks.   
Your'e just not spending an entire evening trying to work out why your sprite blitter doesn't work on a blue back ground on an RTX2000 series.

comments.author: BenTheSodaman
comments.body:
No set definition.

Assholes and dickwads will throw it around on things that were produced by manually without generative AI. Just as pointing it out to said dickwads tends to result in downvotes too, but at least they know.

I've had my writing get called AI slop for saying things like:

\- Dunning Kroeger without the need to look it up

\- making Kevin Bacon references

\- making references to World of Warcraft raids

\- providing genuine feedback to someone's ideas

\- using bulleted lists and headings in my posts

\- drafting posts in Word without turning off auto-correct that loves to turn a hyphen space into an em dash (cause it sucks to lose a long post before you post it)

\- writing too much in a single post that I have to break it into separate posts

And the **lower IQ dipshits** will just lump me in with terms like AI slop or accuse me of using an LLM to write it. And the times where I've used an LLM for public writing is translating or getting an interpretation of a post that Google Translate is having trouble with.

replies.author: BenTheSodaman
replies.body:
However, this is not to be confused with actual constructive criticism where an individual generates output with AI, but that individual does not have the same quality assurance or criticism threshold as who they are sharing the output with.

Like someone launching their online game with a link of 127.0.0. 1 and wanting folks to make an account  to test it for them and dependent what can make their game more fun.

Or having cover art or a featured screenshot of the Six-Fingered Man, but it's not supposed to be the guy that slew Inigo Montoya's father.

Generating UI that has gibberish text (not just typos, but glyphs no human understands).

Or generating images or videos that don't represent any implemented gameplay (if that) and trying to pitch it as the next big thing that nobody has ever seen before.

Or when someone makes it very clear early on they're only doing this to make a quick buck and share a pre-alpha with paid content or most of their posts on the sub are advertisements, whether discrete or blunt about it.

I digress.

The sub-reddit is far more public. You'll frequently get Luddites huddled around ready to beat the shit out of the next post. And occasionally incompetence waltz in to take a piss who generally don't realize what sub-reddit they're in. But they clicked and the algorithm in its infinite wisdom decides to send their ass back here again. And the waltzer is too incompetent to curate their feed to see fewer things they don't want to see, so some of them keep come back when they see the next aigamedev thread that upsets them off.

The Discord linked in the sidebar or the About section near the top has been overall a better place for more constructive or less destructive conversations or side conversations.

The Discord still depends on the topic and the project. They still have standards and it's still not a haven for low effort outputs that have barely been QA'd. And not a place for people looking for a quick buck or to poach compute, but you'll still see the swoop in like those commission artist scam accounts. And you'll still occasionally get folks that don't read the room and think every channel is a place to provide an unsolicited roast (as opposed to constructive criticism without the need to have a Charlie-level roast to go with it). But that hasn't been as bad from what I recall since leadership expanded staffing/moderators.
